purpose: State the direct-head and predecessor-closure cardinality bounds separately and prove their edge cases. Record root's correct redundancy observation without changing the registered RAW.
assumptions: W is a finite set of nonempty complete group strings over one fixed working-unit alphabet A.
C is a fixed finite prefix-free set of nonempty strings. W is a subset of C*. Several entries may share their first unit; no length bound is imposed.
Nontrivial means a code of length>1 is actually consumed in some W parse; unused long entries are irrelevant.
R is the full nonempty closure of W under u,v=u r -> r. H is its first-unit set; F is its one-unit set; T contains a->b for every exact two-unit remainder ab.
d_h counts distinct second units of h-initial R strings. Define d_h=0 if no such second unit exists.
All assertions are conditional on true complete-group boundaries and the fixed working units, not native atomicity or meanings.
preserved_identity: C=A always covers W using at most22 entries. No bound>22 is claimed for the family allowing only used singleton codes.

first_bound.statement: Every compatible C has at least |H| codewords.
first_bound.proof: For each h in H, the first codeword in any legal parse of an h-initial remainder begins with h. Distinct heads require distinct codewords.

direct_nontrivial_head_bound.let: g is the first unit of one actually used multi-unit code.
direct_nontrivial_head_bound.forced_absence: Prefix-freeness implies g is not a singleton code. Consequently g cannot belong to F.
direct_nontrivial_head_bound.case_in_H: When g is in H, every g-initial remainder has length>=2 and its first code has length>=2. Distinct second units therefore require distinct g-initial codes. Other required heads each cost at least one. This is |H|-1+d_g.
direct_nontrivial_head_bound.case_outside_H: When g is outside H, d_g=0. Every H head still costs at least one, and the assumed actually used g-headed code is one additional entry. Thus the bound is |H|+1. The fact that g is not a remainder's first unit does not rule out its use inside an original group.
direct_nontrivial_head_bound.caveat: An outside-H candidate may be impossible for additional reasons, such as occurring only at positions too near an end. This optimistic bound does not assume such reasons away as a constructed witness.

predecessor_bound.local_implication: For a complete two-unit remainder ab, singleton a implies singleton b: first consume a, leaving the complete one-unit remainder b. Contrapositively, non-singleton b requires non-singleton a.
predecessor_bound.N_g: The set containing g and every vertex with a directed T-path to g.
predecessor_bound.forbidden_case: If N_g meets F, this g is impossible.
predecessor_bound.containment: N_g is a subset of K_g. Every proper predecessor along T starts an existing two-unit remainder and hence lies in H; g was explicitly included.
predecessor_bound.required_per_head: For h in N_g, all h-headed codes have length>=2. At least max(1,d_h) such entries are required. For each remaining head in K_g there is at least one required entry.
predecessor_bound.proof: Partition code entries by their first working unit. Those classes are disjoint. Sum the above minimum counts over the required heads. The max handles g outside H; every other N_g member already begins an R remainder. This does not assume the codes are exactly two units long.
predecessor_bound.dominance: Because g lies in N_g and every added term is nonnegative, the predecessor bound is at least the direct-head bound.
predecessor_bound.interpretation: For a global necessary lower bound on nontrivial codebooks, minimize over all possible actually used heads g, including g outside H. A bound exceeding22 excludes the declared small family. A bound at most22 means only not excluded; it is not exact codebook minimality, a parse witness or a reading.

roots_redundancy_observation.statement: For fully quotient-closed R, F is forward-closed under T.
roots_redundancy_observation.proof: If a is in F and ab is in R, the quotient of ab by a is b, which must be in R and hence in F. Repeat along a T-path.
roots_redundancy_observation.consequence: If g is not in F, N_g cannot meet F. Thus after full closure the forbidden-intersection check is redundant with g not in F. It remains useful as an independent consistency check or while working with an unfinished subset of the closure.
roots_redundancy_observation.not_a_new_condition: This does not change either count bound, introduce a new parameter or claim any native result.

sharp_toy.identity: The two singletons a,b cover W.
sharp_toy.nontrivial: If a is singleton, ab forces b singleton. If b is singleton, ba forces a singleton. A nontrivial code therefore contains neither singleton; each two-unit whole word must be its own code.
sharp_toy.attained_minimum: Exactly four codes aa,ab,ba,bb form a prefix-free table and are all used. Thus the nontrivial minimum is4 here, while the unrestricted minimum is2.
sharp_toy.lesson: The elementary necessary bound can be sharp on a finite teaching example; this does not make it the exact minimum for an arbitrary larger panel.

certificate_limits: A derived remainder needs an explicit u,v=u r chain from the fixed complete-group inputs.
Full R closure and the deduced H/F/T/d sets must be independently checkable before they are described as exact.
A partial but valid derivation set can yield a weaker valid necessary bound; it cannot silently be called the full closure.
No guessed source words, per-form arities, source-language lexicon or native values enter the proof.
No source-word-frequency claim follows from the cardinality bound.
No26/28-letter expansion or complete table search is implied by either outcome.
execution: No native strings were queried, no R/H/F/T/d/N values were computed, no decoder or solver was executed, and no1233 artifact was opened. Only own JSON-file syntax/hash validation is performed.
